lessons.title: First-order gradient dynamics must not be claimed as loss-landscape curvature without Hessian or second-order measurement

lessons.title: Floating-point machine epsilon is a relative unit roundoff, not an absolute lower bound on gradient magnitude or noise floor

Conflating machine epsilon with an absolute gradient noise floor is mathematically invalid. Absolute thresholds must be explicitly labeled as numerical regularizers or censoring bounds, not physical properties.

lessons.title: Masked subset gradient contribution under full-batch reduction denominator is not equivalent to an independently normalized subset loss gradient
lessons.failure_pattern: Conflating the masked gradient contribution of a class subset to the full-batch objective with the gradient of an isolated subset loss normalized only by subset pixels
lessons.description: Under PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='mean'), evaluating loss on an isolated class subset yields L_isolated = sum_{i in M} w_{y_i} ell_i / sum_{i in M} w_{y_i}. This causes two critical scientific failures: (1) for any single-class mask (e.g. M_c), w_c cancels identically from numerator and denominator, rendering weighted and uniform losses mathematically identical; and (2) the sum of isolated subset gradients does not equal the full-batch loss gradient (g_rare + g_common + g_other != g_total) because each subset divides by a different scalar denominator. Only by evaluating the masked gradient contribution under the full-batch reduction denominator D_batch = sum_{i in B_valid} w_{y_i} is exact linear decomposition preserved (g_total = sum g_{M_k}) and class-weight scaling w_c / bar{w}_batch retained. Subgradient protocols must explicitly report Estimand A ('masked gradient contribution under the full-batch reduction denominator') and prohibit calling it an unadorned class-specific loss gradient.
lessons.root_cause: Conflating isolated subset loss normalization with linear subgradient decomposition of a full-batch objective.
lessons.detection_method: Audit subgradient equations to assert shared full-batch denominator D_batch, partition completeness, single-class non-cancellation, and precise estimand qualification.
lessons.prevention_method: GOV-RULE-113: Subgradient decompositions must evaluate masked gradient contributions under the shared full-batch reduction denominator D_batch, and must explicitly distinguish masked contribution vectors from isolated subset loss gradients.
lessons.prevention_rule: GOV-RULE-113: Subgradient decompositions must evaluate masked gradient contributions under the shared full-batch reduction denominator D_batch, and must explicitly distinguish masked contribution vectors from isolated subset loss gradients.
lessons.correct_rule: Enforce identical denominator D_batch = sum_{i in B_valid} w_{y_i} across all subset gradient components to guarantee g_total = sum g_{M_k} and retain class-weight scaling.
lessons.preflight_question: Does the subgradient decomposition use the shared full-batch denominator D_batch and explicitly qualify the estimand as a masked gradient contribution?
lessons.notes: Enforces mathematically sound subgradient decomposition and estimand precision.

lessons.title: AdamW parameter update magnitude is governed by adaptive moments and decoupled weight decay, not directly by raw gradient L2 norm
lessons.failure_pattern: Conflating raw gradient L2 norm ||g_t||_2 with AdamW parameter update magnitude ||Delta theta_t||_2 or claiming raw gradient norms directly dictate step displacement
lessons.description: Under AdamW, coordinate update magnitudes are normalized by the running second-moment estimate sqrt(hat{v}_t) + eps and scaled by decoupled weight decay eta * lambda * theta_{t-1}. Raw gradient L2 norm does not directly equal or determine parameter update magnitude; rather, coordinates with persistent large gradients experience automatic second-moment dampening. The raw gradient L2 norm directly determines only whether global gradient clipping activates under torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(max_norm=1.0). In Tier 2, parameter-update measurements must be reported strictly as observed parameter displacement ||theta_t - theta_{t-1}||_2, and protocols must avoid asserting that raw gradient L2 directly governs optimizer step size.
lessons.root_cause: Treating adaptive preconditioned optimizers (AdamW) as if they followed unscaled SGD dynamics where step size is strictly linear in gradient magnitude.
lessons.detection_method: Audit gradient and optimizer prose to assert clear distinction between raw gradient L2 norm, clipped gradient norm, AdamW preconditioned update, and observed parameter displacement.
lessons.prevention_method: GOV-RULE-114: Distinguish raw gradient L2 norm, clipped gradient norm, AdamW preconditioned update, and observed parameter displacement; do not claim raw gradient L2 directly determines AdamW parameter update magnitude.
lessons.prevention_rule: GOV-RULE-114: Distinguish raw gradient L2 norm, clipped gradient norm, AdamW preconditioned update, and observed parameter displacement; do not claim raw gradient L2 directly determines AdamW parameter update magnitude.
lessons.correct_rule: Report raw gradient L2 norm as gradient magnitude and clipping trigger; report parameter update magnitude as actual observed displacement ||Delta theta_t||_2 under AdamW preconditioning.

lessons.notes: Enforces precise mathematical characterization of AdamW dynamics.

lessons.title: Negative gradient cosine similarity denotes opposing instantaneous directional geometry and does not prove destructive interference or optimization failure without paired intervention
lessons.failure_pattern: Overinterpreting negative cosine similarity cos(g_rare, g_common) < 0 as proof of destructive interference, harmful conflict, or training failure
lessons.description: Under linear subgradient decomposition, a negative cosine similarity indicates that two masked gradient contributions point in opposing directions in parameter space at that instantaneous checkpoint. In multi-task or multi-class learning, opposing gradient vectors are an expected geometric feature of non-aligned loss surfaces and do not alone prove impaired optimization, degraded validation mIoU, or causal failure. Wording such as destructive interference, harmful conflict, antagonism, or destabilizing overclaims causality. The strongest defensible claim from instantaneous profiling is strictly opposing gradient direction; claims of causal failure require paired dynamic trajectory evidence from Tier 2 intervention.
lessons.root_cause: Inferring causal optimization failure from instantaneous static directional geometry.
lessons.detection_method: Scan protocol markdown and JSON for prohibited causal tokens (destructive interference, harmful conflict, antagonism, destabilizing) and assert strictly opposing gradient direction terminology.
lessons.prevention_method: GOV-RULE-115: Use strictly opposing gradient direction for negative cosine observations; prohibit claims of destructive interference, harmful conflict, or causal failure without paired dynamic training evidence.
lessons.prevention_rule: GOV-RULE-115: Use strictly opposing gradient direction for negative cosine observations; prohibit claims of destructive interference, harmful conflict, or causal failure without paired dynamic training evidence.
lessons.correct_rule: Restrict negative cosine interpretation to instantaneous opposing gradient direction in parameter space, reserving causal claims for paired intervention outcomes.
lessons.preflight_question: Is negative cosine similarity described strictly as opposing gradient direction rather than destructive interference or optimization failure?
lessons.notes: Prevents unverified causal overclaims from static geometry.

lessons.title: Deterministic full-dataset traversal represents a physical census and must not be conflated with the stochastic Candidate F sampling distribution

lessons.description: Evaluating minibatches by sequential deterministic traversal across all 132 TRAIN tiles (33 batches of B=4) constitutes an unconditional full-dataset physical census. It is not representative of the training minibatch distribution produced by the Candidate F dynamic class-conditioned sampler (which draws 72 tiles/epoch with non-uniform class-support probability). Claiming that Population B static profiling reflects Candidate F training dynamics creates an invalid transportability assumption. Protocols must explicitly define Population B as an unconditional full-dataset physical census designed for exhaustive static profiling, while acknowledging that Tier 2 provides the actual Candidate F sampling distribution.

lessons.title: Aggregate class subset gradients are resultant vectors subject to internal multi-class cancellation and cannot be interpreted as uniform individual class directions

Furthermore, Cosine(g_rare, g_common) evaluates alignment against the aggregate resultant vector, not average pairwise class alignment. lessons.title: Deterministic numerical reproducibility within a single environment does not guarantee bitwise identity across heterogeneous hardware or software stacks

lessons.description: In floating-point gradient evaluations, parallel reductions (e.g. cuBLAS, atomicAdd) are non-associative. Setting identical random seeds, inputs, and model parameters ensures deterministic repeated evaluation within a single execution environment, but does not guarantee bitwise identical gradient tensors across different GPU architectures, CUDA versions, or compiler optimization flags. Asserting bitwise identity without qualification is a false reproducibility claim. Protocols must state the exact supported reproducibility guarantee (e.g. single-environment deterministic recomputation under fixed seeds and determinism flags) and avoid claiming universal cross-platform bitwise invariance.

lessons.title: Raw L2 norm and RMS per-parameter scale serve distinct roles and must not be conflated when comparing modules of different parameter counts
lessons.failure_pattern: Comparing raw gradient L2 norms across network layers of differing parameter counts or claiming RMS norm makes layers directly comparable in physical force
lessons.description: Comparing raw gradient L2 norms ||g_l||_2 across network modules with vastly different parameter dimensions d_l produces scale distortions driven by parameter count rather than gradient density. Raw L2 norm represents total physical magnitude in the parameter subspace and dictates clipping activation, whereas RMS norm RMS(g_l) = ||g_l||_2 / sqrt(d_l) provides normalized per-parameter gradient scale suitable for cross-layer depth comparisons. Neither metric alone captures all dynamics: raw L2 must not be claimed to provide direct cross-layer scale equivalence, and RMS must not be claimed to govern total parameter displacement or optimizer clipping. Protocols must explicitly define raw L2 as within-layer physical magnitude and RMS as cross-layer normalized comparison.

lessons.title: Gradient clipping activation must be evaluated at the optimizer accumulation boundary on accumulated gradients, not on unaccumulated per-physical-batch gradients

Global gradient clipping (torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_, max_norm=1.0) is executed exclusively at the optimizer step boundary immediately before optimizer.step(). The norm of an individual physical batch gradient is not the norm entering the optimizer. Reporting clipping activation per physical batch measures a surrogate quantity that misrepresents actual optimizer dynamics. Protocols must evaluate clipping activation indicator I(||g_t^{accum}||_2 > 1.0) strictly at the accumulation boundary on the fully accumulated gradient vector.

lessons.title: Small-sample (n=3) non-significant differences must not be interpreted as proof of no effect or grounds to reject an optimization bottleneck
lessons.failure_pattern: Claiming that a lack of statistically significant difference across 3 random seeds proves the absence of an effect or justifies rejecting a hypothesis

Claiming that trajectories do not differ significantly therefore weighting is rejected as a bottleneck commits a severe inferential error (treating absence of evidence as evidence of absence). Under n=3 paired designs, conclusions must be strictly bounded: report observed effect direction, estimated paired effect size, and uncertainty intervals, and state that no detectable difference was observed under the specific short-horizon protocol while acknowledging that moderate or longer-horizon effects cannot be ruled out.

lessons.title: Dispersion ratios with potentially vanishing denominators require categorical censoring rather than artificial epsilon regularizers
lessons.failure_pattern: Dividing dispersion metrics (such as IQR or median) without defining categorical handling for zero denominators or adding ad-hoc epsilons to force finite ratios

Adding an arbitrary epsilon constant (e.g. + 1e-8) artificially perturbs the metric and creates arbitrary ratio values. Protocols must pre-register categorical handling: if IQR_uniform == 0 and IQR_canonical > 0, categorize as UNDEFINED_ZERO_DENOMINATOR; if both are zero, categorize as BOTH_IQR_ZERO; if either is non-finite, categorize as NONFINITE. Finite ratios and log-dispersion differences are evaluated strictly when both dispersion metrics are strictly positive.

lessons.title: Within-batch cosine similarity cancels the common scalar reduction denominator identically and is altered across weighting arms strictly by numerator vector reweighting
lessons.failure_pattern: Claiming that loss reduction denominator scaling D_batch alters within-batch gradient cosine similarity between subgradient contributions
lessons.description: Under linear subgradient decomposition with a shared full-batch denominator D_batch, both g_rare = (1/D_batch) * sum_{i in M_rare} w_{y_i} grad l_i and g_common = (1/D_batch) * sum_{i in M_common} w_{y_i} grad l_i share the identical positive scalar factor 1/D_batch. In the cosine similarity formula <g_rare, g_common> / (||g_rare|| * ||g_common||), the scalar 1/D_batch cancels identically from numerator and denominator. Therefore, the reduction denominator D_batch has zero effect on within-batch cosine similarity. Altering the loss weighting intervention (canonical vs uniform) shifts cosine similarity exclusively through numerator class reweighting (reorienting the constituent vectors inside g_rare and g_common), not through denominator scaling.
lessons.root_cause: Failing to recognize that positive scalar multiplication of both vectors leaves cosine similarity invariant.
lessons.detection_method: Audit cosine mathematical proofs to assert explicit recognition of denominator scalar cancellation and numerator composition effects.
lessons.prevention_method: GOV-RULE-124: Subgradient cosine analyses must explicitly note that shared positive scalar denominators cancel identically, attributing directional shifts strictly to numerator class reweighting.

lessons.title: Paired inference on within-batch subgradient geometry must aggregate to parent acquisition clusters to prevent batch-level pseudo-replication
lessons.failure_pattern: Applying paired statistical tests (such as Wilcoxon signed-rank) directly to batch-level cosine metrics when multiple batches originate from or share tiles from the same parent acquisition cluster
lessons.description: In OPS-02 TRAIN, all 40 parent acquisition clusters contain between 2 and 4 physical tiles, and 17 clusters contain multiple tiles with dual-class support. Deriving multiple minibatches from these clusters creates nested observations. Running paired hypothesis tests on raw batch-level cosine similarities treats nested observations as independent, committing pseudo-replication and underestimating sampling variance. For H2 directional alignment, raw batch-level distributions are retained strictly for descriptive characterization. Formal paired inference must aggregate batch-level values within each arm to the parent acquisition cluster level (using cluster medians) and evaluate paired contrasts across matched parent clusters (inferential unit = paired cluster summary). Furthermore, formal confirmatory inference is restricted to the primary global full-network contrast, with stage-representative layers treated as secondary descriptive diagnostics.

lessons.detection_method: Audit H2 statistical inference specification to verify that paired Wilcoxon tests operate on paired parent-cluster median summaries rather than raw physical batches, and that stage-representative layers are designated as secondary descriptive diagnostics.
lessons.prevention_method: GOV-RULE-126: Formal hypothesis testing on spatial gradient geometry must use the parent acquisition cluster as the inferential unit (via cluster medians). Raw batches are strictly descriptive units. Multi-layer evaluations must designate the global contrast as primary and layer-wise metrics as secondary descriptive diagnostics.

lessons.title: Raw physical observations for cluster-level paired inference must be cluster-pure to prevent non-identifiable multi-cluster batch mixing

Enforcing B_phys=8 for raw H2 observations forces every physical batch to span multiple parent clusters (100% MULTI_CLUSTER_BATCH), rendering the batch-to-cluster mapping non-identifiable. Assigning multi-cluster batches to a dominant cluster, splitting cosines, or duplicating batches introduces arbitrary weighting and pseudo-replication. To preserve cluster-level paired inference, the raw physical observation unit must be cluster-pure: each observation is a single dual-supported physical tile (or cluster-pure batch of size up to 4 tiles from that cluster). The three-tier hierarchy is strictly: (1) Raw descriptive unit: dual-supported physical tile observation (B_phys=1 or cluster-pure batch); (2) Primary independence unit: parent acquisition mission datatake cluster (K=40); (3) Inferential unit: paired parent-cluster median summary. Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test evaluates cluster-median differences using asymptotic continuity-corrected tie adjustment (or exact permutations when tie-free), with explicit reporting of n_paired, n_zero, and n_effective.

lessons.title: Execution authorization compute ceilings must be mathematically reconciled with deterministic scientific population requirements to prevent population truncation or execution failure
lessons.failure_pattern: Maintaining a stale execution compute ceiling (such as 120 backward passes) when taxonomy or population expansion increases the deterministic backward-pass requirement (such as 178 passes for 28 tiles x 4 passes + 66 H1 passes), creating an unavoidable failure mode where execution either breaches the ceiling or silently truncates the scientific population.
lessons.description: In DIAG-05, earlier design drafts using a 2-class common subset (MCC and IWs) identified 11 dual-supported 4-tile minibatches, corresponding to 44 H2 backward passes and 110 total passes within a 120-pass ceiling. When the protocol transitioned to the authoritative 7-class dynamic phenomena set (Common-7) and cluster-pure tile observations (LL-DIAG05-PLAN-024), the eligible Population-A count expanded to exactly 28 physical tiles across 15 parent clusters. Evaluating 28 tiles with 4 backward passes per tile (rare and common gradients across Control and Treatment arms) deterministically requires 112 H2 backward passes. Adding the 66 H1 census passes yields exactly 178 deterministic backward passes. Retaining a stale ceiling of 120 backward passes creates an operational contradiction: either the execution runner aborts upon exceeding the ceiling, or it is forced into unauthorized ad-hoc subsampling that discards more than half of the eligible population. Execution compute ceilings must be derived directly from the exact population census and pass mechanics, with ceilings strictly >= deterministic requirements.

lessons.prevention_method: GOV-RULE-128: Pre-execution governance must mathematically derive the exact deterministic backward-pass requirement from the registered population census and autograd pass mechanics. The hard execution ceiling must be set strictly greater than or equal to this deterministic requirement, prohibiting silent population truncation or arbitrary subsampling to fit a stale ceiling.
lessons.prevention_rule: GOV-RULE-128: Pre-execution governance must mathematically derive the exact deterministic backward-pass requirement from the registered population census and autograd pass mechanics. The hard execution ceiling must be set strictly greater than or equal to this deterministic requirement, prohibiting silent population truncation or arbitrary subsampling to fit a stale ceiling.
